claim.quote: Here we demonstrate trapping of antihydrogen atoms.

date.note: Nature online publication date; the abstract page gives no earlier preprint date.

key_value_text.quote: we observed 38 annihilation events consistent with the controlled release of trapped antihydrogen from our magnetic trap; the measured background is 1.4 ± 1.4 events
key_value_text.value: 38 annihilation events consistent with the release of trapped antihydrogen; background 1.4 ± 1.4 events

name: Trapped antihydrogen

significance.value: 38 observed events against a measured background of 1.4 ± 1.4 events (no sigma level stated in the abstract)

summary.plain: ALPHA reported that it had held atoms of antihydrogen in a magnetic trap. It saw 38 annihilation events consistent with the controlled release of trapped atoms, against a measured background of 1.4 events.
summary.technical: Trapping of antihydrogen atoms in the ALPHA magnetic trap: from about 10^7 antiprotons and 7 x 10^8 positrons, 38 annihilation events were observed consistent with controlled release of trapped antihydrogen; the measured background is 1.4 ± 1.4 events.

title: Trapped antihydrogen
why_it_matters: The abstract says trapping opens the door to precision measurements on anti-atoms, which can soon be subjected to the same techniques as developed for hydrogen.
